about.label: 01 / ABOUT
about.heading: Hi, I'm Minh Anh
about.copy: I am a 12th-grade student at Vinschool Times City, Hanoi, Vietnam. I am interested in how data and technology can help us better understand human health. This interest arose from the daily challenges I and those around me face, particularly academic stress and sleep, and a desire to find evidence-based solutions. Through founding The Mindful Odyssey and leading VTEC, my school's technology club, I have learned to approach problems with curiosity, responsibility, and a willingness to adjust my ideas when they don't work. I hope to hone my math, programming, and statistical analysis skills to transform data into insights that can support better health decisions.

popups.title: VTEC (Vinschool Technology Club)

image.alt: Award ceremony of Reinvintech 2026, delivered by VTEC

popups.roleDates: Member of the Expertise Department, Sep 2024-Jun 2025 · President, Jun 2025-present

rows.label: Why
rows.text: VTEC is a student-led technology club at Vinschool. I joined to help build a community where students can explore technology together and turn what they learn into practical projects.

rows.label: What I did
rows.list: Judged the VinSTEM robotics challenge and led the VinSTEAM Innovations competition · Helped expand the club to The Harmony campus · Drafted the plan and co-developed content for REINVINTECH, an AI competition focused on well-being · Coordinated with teachers, sponsors, and vendors to deliver SPARKMIND Festival, featuring AI, robotics, and drones

rows.label: Results
rows.list: Around 50 members aged 15-17 across two campuses · Nearly 100 registrations for REINVINTECH, with eight teams completing working products · More than 200 SPARKMIND attendees and over VND 70 million in sponsorship · 150+ VinSTEM participants · 20+ teams in VinSTEAM Innovations · Around 10 former REINVINTECH candidates later applied to join VTEC

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: Project planning · Team coordination · Event delivery · Stakeholder communication · Sponsorship coordination

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: Start with the goal everyone shares, then work toward a practical compromise.

rows.label: Why
rows.text: During exam periods, I saw friends struggling with stress and poor sleep, but there was no regular space at school to practise simple coping strategies together.

rows.label: What I did
rows.list: Co-led a stress-management workshop with a classmate · Started BewellNest with the School Psychology Office, offering weekly 30-minute sessions with light movement, games, and open conversation · Created content for BewellActs, a short daily physical-activity challenge · Began a sleep study to understand student sleep patterns and explore the BewellNest pilot (see Innovation)

rows.label: Results
rows.list: 30 workshop attendees, with 90% rating the session above 8/10 · 20-25 students at a typical BewellNest session · BewellActs reached dozens of students daily · Ranked in the Top 100 out of approximately 5,000 initiatives in Vinschool Well-being Initiatives in two consecutive years

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: Initiative design · Student engagement · Workshop facilitation · Collaboration with school support staff · Communicating well-being ideas

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: A single event raises awareness. Long-term habits need a consistent space to grow.

popups.title: Slumbering

image.alt: Three Slumbering app screens showing nightly goals, morning check-in and the Journey screen

popups.roleDates: Designed and built independently with AI assistance, Jun-Aug 2026

rows.label: Why
rows.text: Many students know what healthy sleep habits look like but find it difficult to follow them consistently. I wanted to design a tool that makes small changes easier to practise without turning missed goals into a source of guilt.

rows.label: What it does
rows.list: An Android app in Vietnamese · Set small nightly goals for bedtime, winding down, or relaxation · Check in each morning · Track streaks and recent nights on the Journey screen · Earn seven badges · View bedtime charts · Play eight sleep sounds · Set three reminders · Keep all data on the device

rows.label: Design choices
rows.list: A missed goal counts as feedback for the next night · Sound files download on first use to keep the app small · After feedback raised questions about the scientific basis and the number of features, I simplified the first version · Each feature has its own screen, and a short onboarding makes the app easier to understand

rows.label: Results
rows.list: Shared publicly and updated in response to user feedback · Tried by several BewellNest members and other students

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: Designing for a specific user group · Simplifying features from feedback · App development with AI assistance · Publishing a release

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: A smaller set of clearly explained features can be more useful than a crowded app.

popups.title: DS-in-the-making

image.alt: SHAP chart ranking the features most linked to insomnia in a public sleep and lifestyle dataset

popups.roleDates: Self-directed projects with AI assistance, Jun 2026-present

rows.label: Why
rows.text: Before analysing my own survey data, I wanted to practise connecting everyday habits with health-related outcomes using public datasets.

items.did: Trained a Random Forest classifier to predict obesity level and evaluated it with five-fold cross-validation
Used SHAP with a Random Forest classifier to examine features linked to insomnia and sleep apnea
items.result: A ranked chart of the most influential features

items.did: Modelled how pre-bedtime screen time relates to REM sleep
items.result: A broad trend, but not reliable for individual predictions

items.did: Used t-tests to explore whether a blue-light filter was linked to less next-day fatigue among high-brightness phone users
items.result: A line chart comparing fatigue with the filter on and off

items.did: Compared XGBoost and Random Forest models for predicting next-day fatigue
items.result: The XGBoost model reached R² ≈ 0.83, explaining about 83% of the variation in next-day fatigue in this dataset

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: Data cleaning · Classification and regression models · Cross-validation · Explaining models with SHAP · t-tests

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: Public datasets often arrive tidy. Real survey responses need much more careful cleaning.

popups.title: Petite

image.alt: Petite, a pixel-art pet with a reminder speech bubble on a Windows desktop

popups.roleDates: Designed and built independently with AI assistance, Jul 2026

rows.label: Vision
rows.text: A lightweight reminder tool dressed as a desktop pet. It is noticeable enough to prompt action and friendly enough to feel less intrusive.

rows.label: What it does
rows.list: A pixel-art cat or dog appears on a Windows desktop with a speech bubble · Customize pets and reminder categories · Set rules for each reminder, including its message, frequency, and active days · Choose OK or Snooze to dismiss or delay a reminder · Runs in the background while keeping all data on the computer

rows.label: Design aim
rows.text: Make reminders pleasant to notice, so taking action feels easier.

rows.label: Results
rows.list: Released on GitHub · I still use Petite to manage my own reminders

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: User-focused design · Customizable reminder logic · Desktop app development with AI assistance

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: A simple tool can be useful when it addresses a specific, everyday problem.

image.alt: Demo of Gesture-game, with hand movements in front of a webcam control a game

rows.label: Why
rows.text: I wanted to explore a playful, practical use for real-time hand tracking.

rows.label: What it does
rows.text: A webcam tracks hand movements and maps selected gestures to keyboard inputs, letting users play games such as Subway Surfers without touching the keyboard.

rows.label: Tools used
rows.list: Python · OpenCV for the camera feed and image processing · MediaPipe for hand tracking · PyAutoGUI to send keyboard inputs

rows.label: Results
rows.text: A working gesture-controlled input system that maps detected hand movements to directional keys.

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: Real-time hand tracking · Mapping gestures to keyboard input · Combining several Python libraries

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: A familiar technology becomes more interesting when it is applied to a clear, practical use.

popups.title: Sleep quality in middle and high school students and the potential of mindfulness-based group interaction methods

image.alt: Bar chart of the survey sample by grade and gender, before and after the second sampling round

rows.label: Question
rows.text: How well do students sleep, and what role might mindfulness play?

rows.label: Why it matters
rows.text: Members of BewellNest, my mindfulness club, reported sleeping better, but I had not collected evidence to examine that impression. I found that research on adolescent sleep and mindfulness practice in Vietnam was limited, which led me to investigate sleep patterns at my school and pilot a regular mindfulness programme.

rows.label: Who it helps
rows.list: Vinschool students · Secondary and high school students in Vietnam, especially those who struggle with sleep · The wider research field, which has little evidence on Vietnamese adolescents

rows.label: What I did
rows.steps: 1. Reviewed existing studies to identify a research gap and refine the research question · 2. Drafted a research proposal and protocol for a survey and quasi-experimental pilot · 3. Prepared the questionnaire, parent consent form, and student assent form · 4. Surveyed approximately 400 students, then sampled one additional class per grade to address an initial imbalance toward younger students and girls · 5. Ran an eight-week pilot with around 20 BewellNest members, part of The Mindful Odyssey · 6. Cleaned the data and compared patterns by grade and gender

compare.label: What it can show
compare.text: How common self-reported sleep concerns are among students at my school

compare.label: What it can't show
compare.text: Whether BewellNest caused any change, because the pilot is small, sleep is self-reported, and there is no comparison group

rows.label: Role
rows.text: Lead researcher, working with one teammate under the supervision of the School Psychology Office

rows.label: Skills
rows.list: Research-question development · Survey design · Consent and assent procedures · Data cleaning · Descriptive analysis and subgroup comparisons

rows.label: Lesson
rows.text: Convincing evidence depends more on research design than on the amount of data.
